description: CPU usage limit conformance: an MD5 integrity recheck of a 32 GiB legacy Swifty synthetic payload on NVMe, with the widest hash profile, at a 10% limit. Unlimited, this lane uses about a fifth of a 32-thread machine through a pool of about 100 threads that mostly wait on the disk, so the limit has to pace the total rather than each thread. The average must stay at the limit; the busiest 1 s window may exceed it by the start-up burst Windows' 15.6 ms CPU accounting allows before the first bookings land. Copy it with "cpu_usage_limit_percent": null for the unlimited arm and compare the hash time and memory.cpu_machine_* between the two.
notes: Origin: foxy-testkit synthetic --output testkit/origin/data/synthetic-md5-32g --mods 16 --files-per-mod 256 --file-bytes 8388608 --mode swifty --repo-name "TestKit Synthetic MD5 32G" (4112 files, 34 361 166 570 bytes). Memory pressure is pinned to Normal so a busy machine's sampled pressure cannot narrow the hash pool and leave nothing to pace. A BLAKE3 recheck of a real repository on NVMe is disk-bound at a few percent of the machine and never reaches a limit.
